name: Elderberry

facts.what: Ripe black berries, cooked; flower clusters
facts.how: Syrup, jelly, fritters from flowers; never raw in quantity
facts.when: Flowers late spring, fruit June and July
facts.where: Ditches and creek banks with wet feet

caution: Cook the berries: raw fruit, and all stems, leaves, and unripe berries, carry cyanide-producing compounds. Strip berries fully from stems. Learn the shrub confidently in flower before trusting yourself in fruit.

sections.title: Harvesting
sections.body: Snip whole umbels of fully black berries and freeze them; frozen berries rattle off their stems in seconds, which beats an hour of picking.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: Simmered and strained, elderberries make the syrup half of Texas keeps in the fridge by November. The flowers, dipped in batter, fry into lacy fritters.
